text:
maya: Quick question — we're finalizing routing policy UX for tier/region + model-variant fallback. Are we leaning declarative (RoutingPolicy CR) or an imperative eval API? Need to decide before we wire the console panels.

ash: Declarative + stored policy seems nicer for audit/rollouts. We can version them and surface diffs in the console.

simon: +1 for declarative, but we need a simple default policy for tenants who don't touch it. Also: how do we enforce quotas? Hard reject or fall back to cheaper model?

kevin: For free tier we probably want graceful degradation to maintain product experience. Route to smaller/quantized variant and attach a header so apps can show "usage light-mode".

lucy: Enterprise customers will want hard quota enforcement + SLA guarantees. Need per-tenant override flags.

erin: Telemetry question: when we fallback, we must track both the original request's intended model and actual served model, plus cost delta. Console should show "fallback rate" and estimated monthly savings/loss.

maya: Agreed. Sketch of a policy idea:

```yaml
routing_policy:
  id: default-v1
  tiers:
    free:
      prefer: [gpt-lite-1q, gpt-medium-1]
      fallback: [gpt-tiny-4bit]
      quota_behavior: degrade
    pro:
      prefer: [gpt-medium-1, gpt-large-1]
      fallback: [gpt-medium-1-q]
      quota_behavior: throttle
    enterprise:
      prefer: [gpt-large-1]
      fallback: []
      quota_behavior: reject
  region_overrides:
    eu:
      prefer: [gpt-eu-medium]
```

ash: Love it. A few notes: "degrade" should imply both model variant fallback and a token-based meter that can be adjusted. "throttle" means slower processing/queue rather than rejection.

simon: Implementation detail: should we push policy evaluation into the routing tier (edge) or central control plane? Edge helps latency but harder to sync updates.

kevin: Edge + config cache with TTL. If we need immediate kill-switch, control plane should be authoritative with a fast invalidation path.

ops-bot: deploy: routing-config-service v0.6 pushed to staging at 2026-03-18T12:07:01Z :rocket:

lucy: Console UX: two modes. "Quick mode" — dropdowns for tier defaults (fallback strategy: degrade/throttle/reject), per-region toggle. "Advanced mode" — YAML rule editor + validation errors.

erin: Telemetry metrics to add:
- routing.policy.version
- fallback.count (by tier, region, model_from->model_to)
- quota.rejections
- latency.p50/p95 when fallback used
- cost.delta per request

maya: On the internal API debate: simon suggests a RoutingPolicy resource (CRUD). ash suggested an endpoint api.route_eval(request) for dynamic decisions. Can we have both? Store policies as resources and expose an eval endpoint that edge/control-plane calls.

simon: Yeah that would let us keep a cache on the edge and call eval for misses or forced re-eval. Eval returns: {action: route, model: name, reason: fallback|quota|region} 

ash: One more: add response metadata for downstream apps: headers like `x-redwood-routed-model`, `x-redwood-fallback-reason`, and `x-redwood-original-model`.

kevin: Also need a transparent billing hook: mark tokens billed at actual model cost but annotate which billing tier applied (so invoices show fallback adjustments).

lucy: Validation rules we need in console/editor:
- fallback must reference compatible architecture
- no circular fallbacks
- per-region model availability check
- explicit override precedence: tenant override > org policy > default

maya: Action items:
- I will write RFC for RoutingPolicy resource and eval endpoint (assigned: maya, due: 2026-03-25) — link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/452
- simon to prototype edge cache + invalidation (assigned: simon)
- erin to add telemetry counters to the roadmap and mock console panels for fallback metrics (assigned: erin)
- ash/lucy to design Quick vs Advanced console flows (sync Tues)

kevin: Also file an API break-risk note: adding headers may impact clients that rely on strict header schemas. We need a deprecation plan.

maya: Noted. We'll include header opt-in via tenant settings for the first rollout.

ash: Minor nit: quota enforcement semantics should be pluggable — we'll add a small interface: "QuotaStrategy" with implementations degrade/throttle/reject.

simon: P2 risk: telemetry cardinality if we index model_from->model_to tags per request. Keep high-cardinality tags in sampling mode.

erin: For the mock console, I'll include graphs: fallback rate trend, top tenants by fallback frequency, cost impact heatmap by region.

maya: Cool. If nobody objects I'll open the RFC and a staging test plan. We can wire the deploy pipeline to run policy conformance checks pre-deploy.

ash: No objections. :+1:

kevin: Fine with me.

lucy: Let's do it. :rocket:

maya: I'll post the RFC link once created. Thanks everyone.
